title: Numbers, Days and People
intro: This lesson covers the first 30 kanji of the JLRC N5 Kanji Workbook. First come the numbers 一 to 十, then 百, 千 and 万. Next are the sun, the moon and the five elements that name the days of the week (日 月 火 水 木 金 土). Last come 円 (yen), 何 (what), 本 (book) and the people in your family: 人, 男, 女, 子, 父, 母 and 友.

How kanji readings work

Most kanji have two kinds of reading. The workbook calls them the Japanese reading (kun'yomi) and the Chinese reading (on'yomi), and the tables on this page list them as Kun'yomi and On'yomi.

  • The Japanese reading is meaning-based. It is the original Japanese word, and you usually see it when the kanji stands alone or has kana after it, as in 一つ (ひとつ).
  • The Chinese reading is sound-based. You usually see it inside compound words, as in 一月 (いちがつ). The tables write it in katakana.
  • Some words have a special reading that follows neither pattern, such as 一日 (ついたち), 二十日 (はつか) and 日本 (にほん). The workbook marks these with a star, and the word tables here say special reading.
  • Strokes are written from left to right and from top to bottom. The Strokes column gives the number the workbook shows.
  • N5 covers about 100 to 150 kanji, so these 30 are a solid start.

一 (one)

MeaningOn'yomiKun'yomiStrokes
oneイチひと1

One flat stroke, the simplest kanji of all. Before a counter the reading shortens to いっ, as in 一分 (いっぷん) and 一本 (いっぽん).

The 1st of the month is a special reading, ついたち, and it is different from いちにち, which means one whole day.

MeaningOn'yomiKun'yomiStrokes
threeサンみ3

Three flat strokes, with the middle one the shortest. Count the lines and you have the number.

Counting things is みっつ and the 3rd of the month is みっか. In most other words it is さん, and it changes the next sound: 三本 (さんぼん), 三百 (さんびゃく) and 三千 (さんぜん).

fourシよ, よん5

A box with two short strokes hanging inside it. It has five strokes, not four, so count carefully when you write it.

It has three readings. よん is the plain number, よ is in よにん and よっつ, and し is in しがつ (April).

Four strokes: a top bar, a short downward stroke, a bar that turns, and a flat base. The shape is a bit like a number 5 with a flat bottom.

The sound changes with the number in front: 三百 (さんびゃく), 六百 (ろっぴゃく), 八百 (はっぴゃく). It stays ひゃく in 二百, 五百 and 七百.

A short box with one bar across the middle, in four strokes. It is the sun, and also a day.

It has many readings. ひ is the plain Japanese reading, び ends the weekday names, か ends dates like ふつか, にち is in にちようび and 十一日, and じつ is in きゅうじつ.

MeaningOn'yomiKun'yomiStrokes

Three strokes: a post standing on a wide base bar, like a plant growing out of the ground. The lower bar is longer than the upper one.

MeaningOn'yomiKun'yomiStrokes

Four strokes: a frame with a short stroke inside. The yen is named after the round coin.

Say the number first and then 円: 百円 is 100 yen. The Japanese readings まる and まるい mean round, and you do not need them at N5.

Seven strokes: the person radical 亻 on the left and 可 on the right. Think of a person asking what.

なに is used on its own and before か (なにか). なん is used before です and before counters (なんですか, なんぼん, なんにん). The on'yomi カ is rare and you do not need it yet.

MeaningOn'yomiKun'yomiStrokes

Five strokes: a 木 (tree) with an extra bar across its base, which marks the root, the origin. It also means book, and it is the counter for long objects.

The counter changes its sound: いっぽん, にほん, さんぼん, ろっぽん, はっぽん, ひゃっぽん. The Japanese reading もと is rare and you do not need it at N5.

MeaningOn'yomiKun'yomiStrokes

Four strokes: a ハ shape on top of a cross. Picture a father standing with his arms folded.

Use 父 (ちち) for your own father when you talk to other people, and お父さん (おとうさん) for someone else's father. The on'yomi フ is rare and you do not need it yet.

MeaningOn'yomiKun'yomiStrokes

Five strokes: 女 (woman) with two dots inside. The dots are the only difference from 女, and they make it a mother.

Use 母 (はは) for your own mother when you talk to other people, and お母さん (おかあさん) for someone else's mother. The on'yomi ボ is rare and you do not need it yet.

sections.title: Easy to mix up
sections.html:
日, 月, 目 and 白

  • 日 (sun, day) is a short box with one bar in the middle.
  • 月 (moon, month) is taller and narrower, and its left stroke curves.
  • 目 (eye) has two bars inside and 白 (white) has a small slash on top. You meet them later, but they appear as wrong answers in the workbook tests.

人, 入 and 八

  • 人 (person) has two legs that join at the top, and the left stroke is the longer one.
  • 入 (enter) looks the same at first, but the longer stroke is on the right.
  • 八 (eight) has two strokes that never touch.

十, 千 and 土

  • 十 (ten) is a plain cross.
  • 千 (thousand) is 十 with a slanting hat on top.
  • 土 (earth) has two bars, and the lower one is longer.

土 and 士

  • 士 is not one of the 30 kanji here, but it is an easy wrong answer for 土.
  • In 土 the lower bar is the longer one. In 士 the upper bar is longer.

木, 本 and 水

  • 木 (tree) is a trunk with branches and roots.
  • 本 (book) is 木 with an extra bar across the roots.
  • 水 (water) has a hooked stroke down the middle and a splash on each side. 木 has no hook.
  • 休 (rest) is a person beside 木. It is not in this lesson but it often appears as a wrong answer.

水 and 火

  • 水 (water) has a hooked stroke down the middle with drops on both sides.
  • 火 (fire) is a flame with a spark on each side.
  • Both have a small stroke on each side, so check the middle: a hook means water.

女, 母 and 毎

  • 女 (woman) has crossing strokes with no dots.
  • 母 (mother) is 女 with two dots inside.
  • 毎 (every) is 母 with a hat on top. It is in 毎月 (まいつき, every month).

父 and 友

  • 父 (father) has a ハ shape on top of a cross.
  • 友 (friend) has a bar crossed by a slanting stroke, with 又 below.
  • 反 and 刀 look a little like 友, but in 友 the slanting stroke crosses the bar.

男 and 女

  • 男 (man) has a rice field 田 on top of 力 (power).
  • 女 (woman) is the simple kneeling shape on its own.
  • おとこ (man) has no ん, and おんな (woman) has one.

百 and 白

  • 百 (hundred) is 白 (white) with a bar on top.
  • 白 on its own is not in this lesson. If you see the extra bar on top, the number is 100.

子, 字 and 学

  • 子 (child) is the plain shape with three strokes.
  • 字 (letter) and 学 (study) put a roof on top of 子.
  • 好 (like) puts 女 beside 子. You meet all three later.

四, 西, 酒 and 兄

  • 四 (four) is a box with two short strokes inside.
  • 西 (west) has a flat bar across the top, 酒 (alcohol) has the water mark on its left, and 兄 (older brother) has a mouth on top of a person.
  • The workbook uses these three as wrong answers for 四.

万, 千 and 百

  • 万 is 10,000, 千 is 1,000 and 百 is 100.
  • 万 has three strokes and a flat bar on top.
  • 千 has a slanting hat on 十, and 百 has 白 under a bar.
  • Japanese counts in groups of 10,000, so 一万 is 10,000 and 十万 is 100,000.

六 and 八

  • 六 (six) is 八 with a lid on top.
  • 八 (eight) has no lid and its two strokes never touch.

七 and 九

  • 七 (seven) has a flat bar crossed by a stroke that bends to the right at the bottom.
  • 九 (nine) has a slanting stroke crossed by a stroke that bends and hooks.
  • 七 and 十 both have a cross. In 七 the upright stroke bends, and in 十 it is straight.

The readings of 日

  • ひ is the word on its own, as in 日 (sun, day).
  • び ends the weekday names: にちようび, げつようび.
  • か is in the day counts: ふつか, みっか, よっか, ここのか. The 14th is じゅうよっか and the 20th is はつか.
  • にち is in にちようび, じゅういちにち and なんにち. じつ is in きゅうじつ.

火 and 日 are both ひ

  • On their own, 火 (fire) and 日 (sun) are both read ひ, so look at the shape.
  • In the weekdays, 火 is か (かようび, Tuesday) and 日 is にち (にちようび, Sunday).

Three readings of 四

  • よん is the plain number and is in 四十 (よんじゅう) and 四か月 (よんかげつ).
  • よ is in 四人 (よにん), 四つ (よっつ) and 四日 (よっか).
  • し is in 四月 (しがつ, April).

七 and 九 have two readings each

  • 七 is しち in しちがつ and しちじ, and なな in ななつ and ななひゃく.
  • 九 is きゅう in きゅうふん and 九十九, and く in くがつ and くじ.
  • The 7th is なのか and the 9th is ここのか.

The days of the month

  • 1st ついたち, 2nd ふつか, 3rd みっか, 4th よっか, 5th いつか.
  • 6th むいか, 7th なのか, 8th ようか, 9th ここのか, 10th とおか.
  • From the 11th, the ending is usually にち (じゅういちにち), except 14th じゅうよっか and 20th はつか.
  • いちにち means one whole day, but ついたち is the 1st of the month.

Counting pieces: ひとつ to とお

  • ひとつ, ふたつ, みっつ, よっつ, いつつ, むっつ, ななつ, やっつ, ここのつ, とお.
  • Ten is とお, with no つ at the end.
  • These use the Japanese readings. Seven things is ななつ, not しちつ.

20th and 20 years old

  • 二十日 is はつか and means the 20th of the month.
  • はたち means 20 years old. It is written 二十歳, with a different kanji.
  • The workbook uses はたち as a wrong answer for 二十日.

三月 and 三か月

  • 三月 is March (さんがつ). 三か月 is three months (さんかげつ).
  • The か before 月 means a number of months, and 月 is read げつ.
  • Months of the year use がつ. つき on its own is the moon or month, as in まいつき.

何: なに or なん?

  • なに is used on its own and before か, as in 何か (なにか).
  • なん is used before です and before counters: 何ですか, 何本, 何人 (なんにん), 何日.
  • 何人 can also be なにじん, which asks about nationality.

Sound changes after numbers

  • ほん becomes ぼん after 三 and ぽん after 一, 六, 八 and 百 (いっぽん, さんぼん, ろっぽん, はっぽん, ひゃっぽん). After 二 it stays ほん (にほん).
  • ふん becomes ぷん after 一, 六 and 十 (いっぷん, ろっぷん, じゅっぷん). After 二 and 九 it stays ふん.
  • ひゃく becomes びゃく after 三 and ぴゃく after 六 and 八 (さんびゃく, ろっぴゃく, はっぴゃく).
  • せん becomes ぜん after 三 (さんぜん), and 八 shortens to はっ (はっせん).

Counting people: ひとり to にん

  • ひとり (1) and ふたり (2) are special readings.
  • From three people on, add にん: さんにん, よにん, ひゃくにん. Four is よにん, not よんにん.
  • Nationality uses じん: にほんじん, がいこくじん.

日本: にほん or にっぽん?

  • 日本 is read にほん in everyday speech. にっぽん is also correct and is used in some formal and official uses.
  • 二本 (two long objects) is also にほん, so use the sentence to tell them apart.

My family and your family

  • 父 (ちち) and 母 (はは) are for your own parents when you talk to other people.
  • お父さん (おとうさん) and お母さん (おかあさん) are for someone else's parents.
  • Both お words have a long vowel: おとうさん, おかあさん.

男 and 女 words

  • 男 and 女 are おとこ and おんな on their own.
  • In longer words they are だん and じょ: 男せい (だんせい), 女せい (じょせい), 男子 (だんし), 女子 (じょし).
  • 男の子 is おとこのこ (boy) and 女の子 is おんなのこ (girl).

Parts A to D follow the exercises in the Kanji Workbook N5, Lessons 1 to 3. The workbook's own answer key was not available, so these answers were worked out from the lessons and the word lists. They are model answers, not the official answer key. If one differs from the workbook's key, trust the workbook.

Part A: Read the kanji words

#AnswerWhy
1ひとつOne piece is ひとつ. Counting small things uses the Japanese readings.
2ふたつTwo pieces is ふたつ.
3みっつThree pieces is みっつ, with a small っ.
4じゅうろく十 is じゅう and 六 is ろく, so 16 is じゅうろく.
5ごじゅうはちIt is 五 (ご), 十 (じゅう) and 八 (はち), so 58 is ごじゅうはち.
6よっつFour pieces is よっつ, with a small っ.
7しちじ7 o'clock is しちじ. Telling the time uses しち here, not なな.
8くがつSeptember is くがつ. The 九 is く here, not きゅう.
9はっぽん八 shortens to はっ before ぽん, so 8 long objects is はっぽん.
10じゅっぷん十 shortens to じゅっ before ぷん, so 10 minutes is じゅっぷん.
11もくようびThursday is もくようび. 木 is もく in the weekday.
12きんようびFriday is きんようび.
13いっかげつ一 shortens to いっ before かげつ, so 1 month is いっかげつ.
14よんかげつ4 months is よんかげつ.
15せんはっぴゃく1,000 is せん and 800 is はっぴゃく, so 1,800 is せんはっぴゃく.
16さんまんろくせん30,000 is さんまん and 6,000 is ろくせん, so 36,000 is さんまんろくせん.
17みずOn its own, 水 is みず. The すい is for すいようび.
18いちがつじゅうよっかJanuary is いちがつ and the 14th of the month is じゅうよっか.
19しがつふつかApril is しがつ and the 2nd of the month is ふつか.
20しちがつはつかJuly is しちがつ and the 20th of the month is はつか.
21なんにん何 becomes なん before a counter, so how many people is なんにん.
22おとうさんSomeone else's father is おとうさん, with a long う.
23おかあさんSomeone else's mother is おかあさん, with a long あ.
24ともだちFriend is ともだち.
25にほんじんJapan is にほん and 人 is じん after a country, so a Japanese person is にほんじん.
26さんにんThree people is さんにん.
27ひとりOne person is ひとり, a special reading.
28おとこのこA boy is おとこのこ.
29おんなのこA girl is おんなのこ.
30ははYour own mother is はは.

Part B: Write the words in kanji

#AnswerWhy
1五ついつつ means 5 pieces.
2九つここのつ means 9 pieces.
3四十よんじゅう means 40. 四 is よん here and 十 is じゅう.
4十一じゅういち means 11. Write 十 and then 一.
5二つふたつ means 2 pieces.
6二十七にじゅうなな means 27. Write the tens first and then the ones: 二, 十, 七.
7六十三ろくじゅうさん means 63. Write 六, 十, 三.
8六つむっつ means 6 pieces.
9十とお means 10 pieces. There is no つ after 十 when it is read とお.
10一日ついたち means 1st day of the month. It is a special reading that you have to memorize. いちにち is different and means one whole day.
11二百にひゃく means 200.
12九千きゅうせん means 9,000.
13五万ごまん means 50,000.
14四万六千よんまんろくせん means 46,000. Write 四万 and then 六千.
15八千二十はっせんにじゅう means 8,020. Write 八千 and then 二十.
16お金おかね means money. The polite お goes in front of 金.
17六月ろくがつ means June.
18十二月じゅうにがつ means December. Write 十, 二, then 月.
19月よう日げつようび means Monday. 月 is the moon. In this workbook よう stays in hiragana.
20五か月ごかげつ means 5 months. The か stays in hiragana between the number and 月.
21父ちち means (my) father.
22本ほん means book.
23三本さんぼん means 3 long objects.
24百本ひゃっぽん means 100 long objects.
25二人ふたり means 2 people.
26四人よにん means 4 people.
27百人ひゃくにん means 100 people.
28子どもこども means child. The ども stays in hiragana.
29千円せんえん means 1,000 yen.
30一万円いちまんえん means 10,000 yen. Say the number first, then 円.

Part C: Choose the right reading

#AnswerWhy
1(c) みっつThree pieces is みっつ. いつつ is five, よっつ is four and ふたつ is two.
2(a) きゅうじゅうきゅう99 is きゅう, じゅう, きゅう. The other choices drop or shorten a sound.
3(c) はちじゅう80 is はちじゅう. Do not forget the long う in じゅう.
4(b) ろっぽん六 becomes ろっ before ぽん. むっ and むい belong to むっつ and むいか.
5(d) とおかThe 10th of the month is the special reading とおか.
6(a) はつかThe 20th of the month is the special reading はつか. はたち means age 20.
7(a) むっつSix pieces is むっつ. やっつ is eight and よっつ is four.
8(d) くSeptember is くがつ, so 九 is く here. きゅう is the plain number.
9(c) やっつEight pieces is やっつ. むっつ is six and よっつ is four.
10(a) ひとりOne person is the special reading ひとり. ふたり is two people.
11(b) すいようびWednesday is すいようび, and the last sound is び in every weekday.
12(b) さんぜん3,000 is さんぜん, because せん becomes ぜん after 三.
13(d) ひOn its own, 火 is ひ. か is used in words like かようび (Tuesday).
14(d) みずOn its own, 水 is みず.
15(a) きOn its own, 木 is き.
16(c) ひゃくまん1,000,000 is ひゃくまん, from 百 (100) and 万 (10,000).
17(a) つき毎月 is まいつき. げつ and がつ are used in other words, such as げつようび and いちがつ.
18(c) しがつApril is しがつ. The 四 is し here, not よん.
19(d) どようびSaturday is どようび.
20(c) ふつかThe 2nd of the month is the special reading ふつか.
21(c) ごひゃくえん500 is ごひゃく, and yen is えん. The other choices change a sound wrongly.
22(b) なんぼん何 becomes なん before a counter, and 本 becomes ぼん after なん.
23(d) おとうさんSomeone else's father is おとうさん, with the long う.
24(a) ともだちFriend is ともだち. 友 is とも.
25(a) にほんJapan is にほん here, with a plain ほ.
26(c) なんにんThe question asks how many students, so it is なんにん. なにじん would ask about nationality.
27(a) おとこのこBoy is おとこのこ. おんなのこ is girl.
28(a) ふたりTwo people is the special reading ふたり.
29(d) ははYour own mother is はは. ちち is father.
30(a) ちちYour own father is ちち. はは is mother.

Part D: Choose the right kanji

#AnswerWhy
1(d) 四つFour pieces is 四つ. 兄, 西 and 酒 look a little like it but mean other things.
2(c) 七月July is 七月, with 七 (seven).
3(b) 五つFive pieces is 五つ.
4(d) 七つSeven pieces is 七つ.
5(d) 一日The 1st of the month is 一日.
6(a) 五十50 is 五十, with 五 (five) and 十 (ten).
7(b) 四人Four people is 四人.
8(a) 四月April is 四月.
9(c) 九日The 9th of the month is 九日.
10(d) 三日The 3rd of the month is 三日.
11(a) 月よう日Monday uses 月, the moon.
12(b) お金Money is お金. 金 is the kanji for gold and money.
13(c) 三百300 is 三百. 百 is 白 with a bar on top.
14(a) 木よう日Thursday uses 木, the tree.
15(c) 土Earth is 土, and its lower bar is the longer one. 士 has the longer bar on top.
16(b) 八千8,000 is 八千.
17(c) 日The day of the test is 日. 火 is fire.
18(b) 水よう日Wednesday uses 水, water.
19(a) 三か月Three months is 三か月. 三月 is March.
20(d) 十日The 10th of the month is 十日. 十月 is October.
21(b) 百本100 long objects is 百本.
22(a) 男Man is 男. 女 is woman.
23(c) お母さんMother is 母. 父 is father.
24(c) 友だちFriend is 友だち. In 友 the slanting stroke cuts through the top bar, and 反 and 刀 are look-alikes.
25(b) 子どもChild is 子. 字, 学 and 好 add extra parts.
26(c) 日本Japan is 日本. 二本 is also read にほん, but it means two long objects.
27(a) 二人Two people is 二人.
28(b) 何日What day is 何日, with 日 for day.
29(d) 千円1,000 yen is 千円.
30(b) 女の子Girl is 女の子.

Part E: Choose the meaning

#AnswerWhy
1(c) ten thousandJapanese counts big numbers in groups of 10,000, so 万 is ten thousand.
2(b) yen円 is the yen, and it also means round.
3(b) what何 asks what, as in なにか and なんですか.
4(b) holiday休日 is a day off, read きゅうじつ.
5(c) foreigner外国 is a foreign country and 人 is person, so a foreign person.
6(b) every month毎 means every, so 毎月 is every month.
7(c) this month今 means now, so 今月 is this month.
8(d) man, male男せい is a man, read だんせい.
9(c) friend友人 is a more formal word for friend, read ゆうじん.
10(b) 3rd floor三がい is the 3rd floor, read さんがい.
11(a) volcano火山 is a fire mountain, a volcano.
12(c) a fire (the accident)火事 is a fire that causes damage, read かじ.
13(c) moneyお金 is money, read おかね.
14(b) 3 monthsか月 counts months, so 三か月 is three months. 三月 is March.
15(d) something何か is something, read なにか.
16(c) child子ども is a child, read こども.
17(d) boy男の子 is a boy, read おとこのこ.
18(b) Japanese person日本人 is a Japanese person, read にほんじん.

Part F: Spot the look-alike kanji

#AnswerWhy
1(b) 百百 is 白 (white) with a bar on top.
2(c) 子子 is the plain shape. 字 and 学 add a roof, and 好 adds 女.
3(b) 土In 土 the lower bar is longer. 士 is the other way round.
4(c) 母母 is 女 with two dots inside. 毎 has a hat on top, and 父 means father.
5(b) 友In 友 the slanting stroke cuts through the top bar.
6(c) 男男 is 田 on top of 力. 女 means woman.
7(b) 本本 is 木 with a bar across the roots.
8(b) 水水 has a hooked stroke in the middle and a splash on each side.
9(b) 火火 looks like a flame with a spark on each side.
10(a) 人人 has its two legs joined at the top, with the longer stroke on the left. 八 has two strokes that never touch. 入 (enter) has the longer stroke on the right.
11(a) 十十 is a plain cross. 千 has a hat, and 土 has two bars.
12(a) 七七 is like 十 with the upright stroke bent to the right at the bottom.
13(c) 八八 is two strokes that spread apart and never touch.
14(b) 四四 is a box with two short strokes inside. 西 has a flat bar across the top, 酒 has the water mark on its left, and 兄 has a mouth on top of a person.
15(c) 日日 is a short box with one bar in the middle. 月 is taller and curves left, 目 has two bars, and 白 has a slash on top.
16(c) 月月 is taller and narrower than 日, with a hook that curves to the left.
17(b) 千千 is 十 with a slanting hat on top.
18(a) 万万 has a flat bar on top and three strokes in all.

#AnswerWhy

title: Time, Seasons and Directions
intro: This lesson covers kanji 31 to 60 of the JLRC N5 Kanji Workbook. Kanji 31 to 40 are the language of time: half, minutes, hours, weeks and years, plus the words for this, last, next and every. Kanji 41 to 50 are the parts of the day, the four seasons and 正 (correct). Kanji 51 to 60 are positions and directions: up, down, left, right, inside, outside and the four points of the compass. Many example words reuse kanji from Kanji 1, like 一, 日, 月 and 人.

The same two kinds of reading from Kanji 1 apply here. The Japanese reading (kun'yomi) is meaning-based and usually appears when a kanji stands alone or has kana after it. The Chinese reading (on'yomi) is sound-based and usually appears inside compound words. As in Kanji 1, the tables write the Chinese reading in katakana.

  • The workbook marks special readings with a star. In this set they are 時けい (とけい), 今年 (ことし), 今日 (きょう), 今朝 (けさ) and 下手な (へたな). The tables write special instead of the star.
  • A reading in square brackets is listed for completeness, but the workbook gives no example words for it, such as [なかば], [チョウ], [カ], [シュン], [トウ], [シュウ], [ホク], [ナン] and [セイ].
  • None means the workbook shows no reading of that kind for the kanji.
  • The Chinese reading column also shows the sound changes you meet inside words, such as プン and ブン for 分.
  • The Strokes column shows the number the workbook gives.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.html:
These are the patterns that show up again and again in this set. Say each table out loud once, then cover the Kana column and test yourself.

Clock times

Add 時 (じ) to the number. Three hours are traps: 4 o'clock is よじ (not よんじ), 7 o'clock is しちじ (not ななじ) and 9 o'clock is くじ (not きゅうじ).

KanaKanjiRomajiEnglish
いちじ一時ichiji1 o'clock
にじ二時niji2 o'clock
さんじ三時sanji3 o'clock
よじ四時yoji4 o'clock
ごじ五時goji5 o'clock
ろくじ六時rokuji6 o'clock
しちじ七時shichiji7 o'clock
はちじ八時hachiji8 o'clock
くじ九時kuji9 o'clock
じゅうじ十時juuji10 o'clock
じゅういちじ十一時juuichiji11 o'clock
じゅうにじ十二時juuniji12 o'clock
なんじ何時nanjiwhat time

The workbook's examples use 一時, 三時, 四時, 六時, 七時, 八時, 九時, 十時 and 何時. The rest follow the same pattern.

Minutes

Add 分 to the number. The sound is ふん after 2, 5, 7 and 9, and ぷん after 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 何. A small っ appears before ぷん after 1, 6, 8 and 10.

KanaKanjiRomajiEnglish

にふん二分nifun2 minutes
さんぷん三分sanpun3 minutes
よんぷん四分yonpun4 minutes
ごふん五分gofun5 minutes
ろっぷん六分roppun6 minutes
ななふん七分nanafun7 minutes
はっぷん八分happun8 minutes
きゅうふん九分kyuufun9 minutes
じゅっぷん十分juppun10 minutes
さんじゅっぷん三十分sanjuppun30 minutes
はんぶん半分hanbunhalf
なんぷん何分nanpunhow many minutes

Every count that ends in 十, such as 二十分 (にじゅっぷん) and 三十分 (さんじゅっぷん), ends in じゅっぷん. 半分 is the one to watch: it is はんぶん with a ぶ, not はんふん. The workbook shows 一分, 二分, 六分, 十分, 三十分 and 半分. A few of these also have a second reading in everyday speech (七分 as しちふん, 八分 as はちふん, 十分 as じっぷん), but the forms in the table are the ones to learn first.

Clock time or length of time

Without 間, 時 is a point on the clock. With 間 (かん) it counts hours. 半 (はん) always goes last.

KanaKanjiRomajiEnglish

いちじはん一時半ichijihan1:30
いちじかん一時間ichijikan1 hour
いちじかんはん一時間半ichijikanhanan hour and a half
さんじはん三時半sanjihan3:30
さんじかんはん三時間半sanjikanhan3 and a half hours

How long: hours, weeks and years

Add 間 to a count to say how long something lasts. 週間 counts weeks and 年間 counts years. Two readings need care: 一週間 has a small っ (いっしゅうかん), and 四年間 is よねんかん, not よんねんかん or しねんかん.

KanaKanjiRomajiEnglish
いちじかん一時間ichijikan1 hour
にじかん二時間nijikan2 hours
なんじかん何時間nanjikanhow many hours
いっしゅうかん一週間isshuukan1 week
にしゅうかん二週間nishuukan2 weeks
さんしゅうかん三週間sanshuukan3 weeks
いちねんかん一年間ichinenkan1 year
にねんかん二年間ninenkan2 years
さんねんかん三年間sannenkan3 years
よねんかん四年間yonenkan4 years
ごねんかん五年間gonenkan5 years

Months use か月 (かげつ), which you learned in Kanji 1, as in 三か月 (さんかげつ). Days use 日間, as in 五日間 (いつかかん, 5 days), which appears in the workbook's exercises.

Last, this, next and every

Look at the middle kanji of each word and you can read the time. 先 means last, 今 means this, 来 means next and 毎 means every.

UnitLast (先)This (今)Next (来)Every (毎)
Week先週 せんしゅう今週 こんしゅう来週 らいしゅう毎週 まいしゅう

Three oddities: 今年 is ことし (special), 毎月 is まいつき (not まいげつ) and 毎年 is まいとし (not まいねん). Also, 今月 is こんげつ and not こんつき.

Parts of the day

午 is noon. 前 (before) and 後 (after) are measured from noon, so 午前 is before noon and 午後 is after noon. 午前 and 午後 go in front of the hour: 午前九時 (ごぜんくじ) is 9 a.m. and 午後三時 (ごごさんじ) is 3 p.m.

Seasons

The workbook lists the seasons in the usual Japanese order, 春夏秋冬 (spring, summer, autumn, winter). Add 休み (やすみ) to a season for its school break.

New Year is 正月 (しょうがつ, shougatsu), and the New Year holidays are 正月休み (しょうがつやすみ).

The exit kanji is 口 (くち), which becomes ぐち in these words. The workbook does not teach it yet, so its exercises sometimes write the word as 北ぐち or 西ぐち.

Special readings

The workbook marks these with a star. They follow no pattern, so memorize them as whole words.

sections.title: Easy to mix up
sections.html:
千, 午 and 年 (thousand, noon and year)

  • 千 (thousand, from Kanji 1) is a slanted hat over a single bar.
  • 午 (noon) has two bars under its hat.
  • 年 (year) has six strokes and is busier than both.
  • 千 was a wrong choice for 午 in the workbook.

先 and 生 (ahead and life)

  • 先 (ahead, last) stands on two legs 儿.
  • 生 (as in 先生, teacher) rests on a long flat bar.
  • 生 was a wrong choice for 先 in the workbook.

前 and 後 (front and back)

  • 前 (front) opens with two dots like a hat and ends with 月 and a small knife 刂.
  • 後 (back) has the step radical 彳 on its left side.

間, 門, 聞 and 問 (interval and the gate kanji)

  • 間 (interval) is 日 inside the gate 門.
  • 聞 puts an ear 耳 in the gate, and 問 puts a mouth 口 in it.
  • The workbook used 門, 聞 and 問 as wrong choices for 間.

夏 and 百 (summer and hundred)

  • 夏 (summer) has a flat bar and a box on top, a bit like 百 (hundred), and it stands on legs 夂.
  • The workbook used 百, 頭 and 頃 as wrong choices.
  • 頭 (head) and 頃 (about) are not taught in this workbook.

春, 夏, 秋 and 冬 (the four seasons)

  • 春 (spring) stacks 三, 人 and 日, with the sun at the bottom.
  • 夏 (summer) is the one with 夂 legs.
  • 秋 (autumn) is grain 禾 next to fire 火.
  • 冬 (winter) is the smallest: 夂 over two small drops.

朝 and 晩 (morning and night)

  • 朝 (morning) has the moon 月 on its right side.
  • 晩 (night) has the sun 日 on its left side.

左, 右 and 石 (left, right and stone)

  • 左 (left) has 工 under the bar and starts with the flat stroke.
  • 右 (right) has 口 under the bar and starts with the slanting stroke.
  • You eat with your right hand, and 口 is the mouth.
  • 石 (stone) has the slanting stroke hanging from the left end of the bar, like a cliff over 口.
  • 石 was a wrong choice for 右 in the workbook.

上 and 下 (up and down)

  • The short mark sits above the long line in 上 (up) and below it in 下 (down).

中 (inside)

  • 中 (inside) is a box 口 with a line straight through the middle.

外, 夕 and 多 (outside and its parts)

  • 外 (outside) is 夕 and ト side by side.
  • 夕 and ト were wrong choices in the workbook because they are its two halves.
  • 多 is 夕 twice.

北 and 南 (north and south)

  • 北 (north) looks like two people back to back.
  • 南 (south) starts with a cross 十 on top of a frame.

東, 木, 来 and 米 (east, tree, come and rice)

  • 東 (east) is the sun 日 inside a tree 木.
  • 木 (tree) is plain.
  • 来 (come) looks like 米 (rice) with the top dot stretched into a flat bar.

西, 四 and 酒 (west, four and sake)

  • 西 (west) has a flat lid over a box.
  • 四 (four, from Kanji 1) is a box with two short legs inside.
  • 酒 (sake) has the water mark on its left side.

正 and 止 (correct and stop)

  • 正 (correct) is 止 (stop) with a flat bar on top.

毎 and 母 (every and mother)

  • 毎 (every) is 母 (mother, from Kanji 1) with a small hat on top.

Readings of 今 (now): いま, こん, きょう, けさ

  • いま on its own.
  • こん in 今週, 今月 and 今晩.
  • 今日 is きょう, 今朝 is けさ and 今年 is ことし.

Readings of 朝 (morning): あさ, けさ

  • あさ in 毎朝 (まいあさ).
  • けさ only in 今朝.

Readings of 日 (sun, day): にち, きょう, か

  • にち in 毎日 (まいにち) and 一日中 (いちにちじゅう).
  • きょう in 今日.
  • か in 五日間 (いつかかん).
  • See the Kanji 1 table for the rest.

Readings of 月 (moon, month): げつ, つき

  • げつ in 今月, 先月 and 来月.
  • つき in 毎月 (まいつき).

Readings of 年 (year, age): ねん, とし, ことし

  • ねん in 来年 and 一年間.
  • とし in 毎年 (まいとし).
  • 今年 is ことし.

Readings of 時 (time): じ, じかん, とき, とけい

  • じ is o'clock (四時 よじ).
  • じかん is how many hours (四時間 よじかん).
  • とき on its own.
  • 時けい is とけい.

Readings of 四 (four): よ, よん, し

  • よ in 四時 (よじ) and 四年間 (よねんかん).
  • よん in 四分 (よんぷん).
  • し in 四月 (しがつ).

Readings of 分 (division, minutes): ふん, ぷん, ぶん, わ

  • ふん after 2, 5, 7 and 9.
  • ぷん after 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 何.
  • ぶん in 半分.
  • わ in 分かる.

Readings of 半 (half): はん

  • 半分 is はんぶん.
  • The ぶん belongs to 分, not 半.
  • 一時半 is いちじはん.

Readings of 週 (week): しゅう

  • 一週間 is いっしゅうかん with a small っ, but 二週間 is にしゅうかん without one.

Readings of 間 (interval): かん, あいだ

  • かん after a count (一時間, 二週間, 四年間).
  • あいだ on its own, as in 銀行の間 (between).

Readings of 先 (ahead, last): さき, せん

  • さき in 先に.
  • せん in 先生, 先週 and 先月.

Readings of 来 (come, next): く, き, らい

  • く in 来る.
  • き in 来ます.
  • らい in 来週, 来月 and 来年.

Readings of 中 (inside, middle): なか, ちゅう, じゅう

  • なか on its own.
  • ちゅう in 午前中 and 中国.
  • じゅう in 一日中, 一晩中 and 一年中.

Readings of 前 (front, before): まえ, ぜん

  • まえ on its own and in 名前 (なまえ).
  • ぜん in 午前 (ごぜん).

Readings of 後 (back, after, later): あと, うし, ご

  • あと for later.
  • うしろ for back.
  • ご in 午後 and in ~後 (after).

Readings of 晩 (night): ばん

  • 今晩 is こんばん, 毎晩 is まいばん and 一晩中 is ひとばんじゅう.
  • Always a voiced ば.

Readings of 正 (correct): ただ, しょう

  • ただ in 正しい.
  • しょう in 正月 (しょうがつ).

Readings of 上 (up): うえ, うわ, あ, じょう

  • うえ on its own, うわ in 上着 (うわぎ), あ in 上げる (あげる), じょう in 上手 (じょうず).

Readings of 下 (down): した, さ, へ

  • した on its own, さ in 下げる (さげる), へ in 下手な (へたな).

Readings of 外 (outside): そと, がい

  • そと on its own.
  • がい in 外国, 外出 and 海外 (かいがい).

Readings of 左 and 右 (left and right): ひだり, みぎ, さゆう

  • ひだり and みぎ on their own.
  • Together they are 左右 (さゆう).

Readings of 東 (east): ひがし, とう

  • ひがし for the direction.
  • とう in 東京 (とうきょう).

Readings of 口 (mouth, exit): くち, ぐち

  • The exit is 北口 (きたぐち), not きたくち.
  • Same for 南口, 東口 and 西口.

Readings of 春, 夏, 秋 and 冬 (the seasons)

  • The Chinese readings [しゅん], [か], [しゅう] and [とう] have no example words in the workbook.
  • Focus on はる, なつ, あき and ふゆ.

Opposites and pairs

Learning these in pairs helps, because each member reminds you of the other.

PairKanjiReadings
up and down上 / 下うえ / した
left and right左 / 右ひだり / みぎ
inside and outside中 / 外なか / そと
front and back前 / 後ろまえ / うしろ
north and south北 / 南きた / みなみ
east and west東 / 西ひがし / にし
a.m. and p.m.午前 / 午後ごぜん / ごご
last week and next week先週 / 来週せんしゅう / らいしゅう
spring and autumn春 / 秋はる / あき
summer and winter夏 / 冬なつ / ふゆ
morning and night朝 / 晩あさ / ばん
raise and lower上げる / 下げるあげる / さげる
good at and poor at上手 / 下手なじょうず / へたな

Sound changes

The same piece of a word changes its sound depending on what comes before it. These are the patterns the workbook shows.

PiecePlainChangesExamples
分 (minutes)ふんぷん, ぶん一分 いっぷん, 六分 ろっぷん, 十分 じゅっぷん, 半分 はんぶん
週 (week)しゅういっしゅう一週間 いっしゅうかん
中 (during, all through)ちゅうじゅう午前中 ごぜんちゅう, 一日中 いちにちじゅう, 一晩中 ひとばんじゅう, 一年中 いちねんじゅう

In the workbook's words, 中 is ちゅう in 午前中 and 中国 (ちゅうごく), and じゅう in the "all through" words 一日中, 一晩中 and 一年中.

intro: This lesson covers kanji 61 to 90 of the JLRC N5 Kanji Workbook. Kanji 61 to 70 are describing words: big, small, cheap, high, new, old, long, early, near and bright. Kanji 71 to 80 are amounts, names and colors: few, many, exist, name, color, white, blue, red, tea and black. Kanji 81 to 90 are everyday verbs: write, go, eat, drink, buy, see, be born, rest, go home and sell. Many example words reuse kanji from Kanji 1 and 2, like 人, 日, 年 and 先.

sections.html:
How the readings are shown

The same two kinds of reading from Kanji 1 and 2 apply here. The Japanese reading (kun'yomi) is meaning-based and usually appears when a kanji stands alone or has kana after it. The Chinese reading (on'yomi) is sound-based and usually appears inside compound words. As before, the tables write the Chinese reading in katakana.

  • The workbook marks special readings with a star. In this set they are 大人 (おとな) and 明日 (あした). The tables write special instead of the star.
  • A reading in square brackets is listed for completeness, but the workbook gives no example words for it, such as [ソウ], [サッ], [ショク], [シキ], [ソク], [ハク], [セイ], [セキ], [イン], [バイ], [キ] and [ケ].
  • None means the workbook shows no reading of that kind for the kanji. 茶 has no Japanese reading.
  • The workbook lists 小鳥 (ことり) with the Chinese readings, but こ is a Japanese reading, so the table puts it with the Japanese readings.
  • The Strokes column shows the number the workbook gives.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.html:
These are the patterns that show up again and again in this set. Say each table out loud once, then cover the Kana column and test yourself.

Describing words (い-adjectives)

Most of the kanji from 61 to 80 start an い-adjective. The kanji carries the meaning and the hiragana after it changes when the word changes form: 高い, 高くない, 高かった.

KanaKanjiRomajiEnglish
おおきい大きいookiibig
ちいさい小さいchiisaismall
やすい安いyasuicheap
たかい高いtakaihigh, tall, expensive
あたらしい新しいatarashiinew
ふるい古いfuruiold
ながい長いnagailong
はやい早いhayaiearly
ちかい近いchikainear
あかるい明るいakaruibright, cheerful
すくない少ないsukunaifew, little
おおい多いooimany, a lot

Two pairs share a sound: おおきい (大) and おおい (多) both start with おお, and あかるい (明) and あかい (赤) both start with あか. The kanji tells you which word it is.

Colors

The color words are い-adjectives too. Drop the い to get the color as a noun, as in 青空 (あおぞら, blue sky) and 赤ちゃん (あかちゃん, baby).

しろい白いshiroiwhite
くろい黒いkuroiblack

あおぞら青空aozorablue sky

茶色い is the color of tea (茶) plus 色 (color): ちゃいろい.

sections.title: Easy to mix up
sections.html:
大, 犬, 木 and 本 (big, dog, tree and book)

  • 大 (big) is a person with arms stretched out wide.
  • 犬 (dog) is 大 with an extra dot.
  • 木 (tree, from Kanji 1) has a trunk running down through the middle, and 本 (book) is 木 with a short bar at the root.
  • 犬, 木 and 本 were wrong choices for 大 in the workbook.

小 and 少 (small and few)

  • 小 (small) is three strokes: a hook with a dot on each side.
  • 少 (few, little) is 小 with a slanting stroke added underneath.
  • Size uses 小 (小さい), and amount uses 少 (少し, 少ない). The workbook used 小ない and 少い as wrong answers.

大 and 多 (big and many)

  • Both start with おお: 大きい (おおきい, big) and 多い (おおい, many).
  • 多 is 夕 twice. 大 is the person with arms out.

白, 自, 日 and 月 (white and its look-alikes)

  • 白 (white) is 日 with a short stroke on top.
  • 自 (self) has two bars inside, and 日 (sun) has one.
  • 月 (moon) opens at the bottom left. All three were wrong choices for 白 in the workbook.

新 and 親 (new and parent)

  • 新 (new) has the axe 斤 on its right side.
  • 親 has 見 on its right side. It was a wrong choice for 新しい in the workbook, and it is not taught yet.

古, 石 and 左 (old, stone and left)

  • 古 (old) is 十 over 口.
  • 石 (stone) hangs a slanting stroke off the bar, like a cliff over 口.
  • 左 (left, from Kanji 2) has 工 under the bar.

長 and 高 (long and high)

  • 長 (long) has three short bars on a long post.
  • 高 (high) looks like a tall tower with a roof.
  • Their opposites, 短い (みじかい, short) and 低い (ひくい, low), appeared as wrong choices. They are not taught yet.

明 and 暗 (bright and dark)

  • 明 (bright) is the sun 日 next to the moon 月.
  • 暗 (dark) also has 日 on the left, with 音 on the right. It is not taught yet.
  • 暗るい, 月るい and 目い were wrong choices for 明るい.

色, 免, 声 and 晩 (color and its look-alikes)

  • 色 (color) ends in a curling hook at the bottom.
  • 免, 声 and 晩 (night, from Kanji 2) were wrong choices for 色.

茶, 葉, 花 and 業 (tea and its look-alikes)

  • 茶 (tea) has the grass radical 艹 on top and a person 人 over 木 below.
  • 葉 (leaf) and 花 (flower) also have 艹 on top. 業 does not. None of them are taught yet.

青, 赤, 白 and 黒 (the four colors)

  • 青 (blue) ends with 月 at the bottom.
  • 赤 (red) ends with legs that spread out.
  • 白 (white) is 日 with a stroke on top.
  • 黒 (black) is 里 with four dots underneath, like fire.

書, 行, 見 and 生 (write and the verbs it was mixed with)

  • 書 (write) has a brush 聿 over 日.
  • 行 (go) is two step radicals side by side.
  • 見 (see) is an eye 目 on two legs.
  • 生 (life) is a plant growing out of the ground. The workbook mixed all four as choices for かきます and いきます.

食, 飲, 飯 and 次 (eat and drink)

  • 食 (eat) is a lid over a bowl.
  • 飲 (drink) is 食 on the left with an open mouth 欠 on the right.
  • 飯 (meal) and 次 (next) were wrong choices. They are not taught yet.

買, 貝, 員 and 見 (buy and the shell kanji)

  • 買 (buy) is a net 罒 over a shell 貝. Shells were once used as money.
  • 貝 is a shell on its own, 員 has a mouth on top, and 見 has an eye on legs.

売, 読, 買 and 借 (sell and its partners)

  • 売 (sell) has 士 on top.
  • 読 (read) is the speech radical 言 next to 売.
  • 買 (buy) is the opposite of 売.
  • 借 (borrow) was a wrong choice. It is not taught yet.

休 and 体 (rest and body)

  • 休 (rest) is a person 亻 leaning on a tree 木.
  • 体 (body) is a person next to 本. It was a wrong choice for 休み.

帰, 掃, 侵 and 浸 (go home and its look-alikes)

  • 帰 (go home) has a short vertical pair on the left.
  • 掃 has the hand radical 扌, 侵 has the person radical 亻 and 浸 has water 氵. None of them are taught yet.

生, 先, 失 and 洗 (life and its look-alikes)

  • 生 (life) rests on a long flat bar.
  • 先 (ahead, from Kanji 2) stands on two legs 儿.
  • 失 and 洗 were wrong choices. They are not taught yet.

Readings of 大 (big, large): おお, おとな, だい, たい

  • おお in 大きい and 大雨.
  • だい in 大学 and 大学生, but たい in 大切な.
  • 大人 is おとな.

Readings of 小 (small): ちい, お, こ, しょう

  • ちい in 小さい, お in 小川 (おがわ) and こ in 小鳥 (ことり).
  • しょう in 小学校.

Readings of 安 (cheap, safe): やす, あん

  • やす in 安い and 安売り.
  • あん in 安ぜんな.

Readings of 高 (high): たか, こう

  • たか in 高い.
  • こう in 高校 and 高校生.

Readings of 新 (new): あたら, しん

  • あたら in 新しい.
  • しん in 新聞.

Readings of 古 (old): ふる, こ

  • ふる in 古い and 古本.
  • こ in 中古車.

Readings of 長 (long, chief): なが, ちょう

  • なが in 長い.
  • ちょう in 校長, 社長 and 会長.

Readings of 近 (near): ちか, きん

  • ちか in 近い.
  • きん in 近じょ.

Readings of 明 (bright): あか, あした, めい

  • あか in 明るい.
  • めい in せつ明.
  • 明日 is あした.

Readings of 少 (few, little): すこ, すく, しょう

  • すこ in 少し and すく in 少ない.
  • しょう in 少年 and 少女.

Readings of 多 (many): おお, た

  • おお in 多い.
  • た in 多分 and 多少.

Readings of 有 and 名 (exist and name): ゆう, めい, な

  • 有名な is ゆうめいな: ゆう for 有 and めい for 名.
  • な in 名前 (なまえ).

Readings of 黒 (black): くろ, こく

  • くろ in 黒い.
  • こく in 黒ばん.

Readings of 書 (write): か, しょ

  • か in 書く and 書き方.
  • しょ in 読書 and 書道.

Readings of 行 (go): い, こう

  • い in 行く.
  • こう in 銀行.

Readings of 食 (eat): た, しょく

  • た in 食べる and 食べもの.
  • しょく in 食事 and 食どう.

Readings of 見 (see): み, けん

  • み in 見る and 見せる.
  • けん in 見学.

Readings of 生 (life): う, せい, じょう

  • う in 生まれる.
  • せい in 先生, 学生 and 一年生.
  • じょう in たん生日 (たんじょうび).

Readings of 休 (rest): やす, きゅう

  • やす in 休む, 休み and 夏休み.
  • きゅう in 休日.

Readings of 売 (sell): う, ばい

  • う in 売る, 売り切れ and 安売り.
  • ばい in 売店.

title: Verbs, Words and Places in Town
intro: This lesson covers kanji 91 to 120 of the JLRC N5 Kanji Workbook. Kanji 91 to 100 are verbs about moving and doors: enter, exit, stop, cut, stand, hold, wait, close, open and hear. Kanji 101 to 110 are about knowing and words: know, study, meet, wear, use, make, say, language, talk and read. Kanji 111 to 120 are places around town: store, school, country, house, car, road, station, capital, metropolis and direction. Many example words reuse kanji from Kanji 1 to 3, like 大, 高, 新 and 売.

How the readings are shown

The same two kinds of reading from Kanji 1 to 3 apply here. The Japanese reading (kun'yomi) is meaning-based and usually appears when a kanji stands alone or has kana after it. The Chinese reading (on'yomi) is sound-based and usually appears inside compound words. As before, the tables write the Chinese reading in katakana.

  • This set has no special (starred) readings.
  • A reading in square brackets is listed for completeness, but the workbook gives no example words for it, such as [リツ], [ジ], [タイ], [ヘイ], [カイ], [チ], [チャク] and [みやこ].
  • The workbook also lists ハイ for 閉. Dictionaries give only ヘイ, and neither appears in an N5 word.
  • None means the workbook shows no reading of that kind. 校, 駅 and 京 have no Japanese reading.
  • A reading followed by a word in brackets, like いり (in いりぐち), only appears in that word.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.html:
These are the patterns that show up again and again in this set. Say each table out loud once, then cover the Kana column and test yourself.

Verb pairs: doing it, or it happens

Several kanji in this set start two verbs. The verb with を is something you do to a thing: ドアを しめます, I close the door. The verb with が happens by itself: ドアが しまります, the door closes.

あける開けるakeruto open (something)
あく開くakuto open (by itself)

はいる入るhairuto enter
だす出すdasuto take out
でる出るderuto leave, to come out

開く is あく here, the door opens. 聞く (ask, hear) looks similar but is きく.

Everyday verbs

sections.title: Easy to mix up
sections.html:
入, 人 and 八 (enter, person and eight)

  • 入 (enter) has its right stroke start higher, with the left stroke leaning on it.
  • 人 (person, from Kanji 1) has the longer stroke on the left.
  • 八 (eight) has two strokes that do not touch.
  • 人 and 木 were wrong choices for 入ります in the workbook.

出, 山, 止 and 正 (exit and its look-alikes)

  • 出 (exit) is like two 山 (mountain) stacked, with one line down the middle.
  • 止 (stop) and 正 (correct, not taught yet) were also wrong choices for 出かけます.

止, 上, 下 and 正 (stop and its look-alikes)

  • 止 (stop) has a short stroke on the left and a tall one in the middle.
  • 上 (up) and 下 (down) are from Kanji 2.
  • 正 is 止 with a bar on top. It is not taught yet.

切, 七, 刀 and 比 (cut and its parts)

  • 切 (cut) is 七 (seven) with 刀 (knife) on the right.
  • 七, 比 and 刀 alone were wrong choices for 切りました.

立 and 位 (stand)

  • 立 (stand) is a person standing on the ground.
  • 位 adds the person radical 亻. It was a wrong choice for 立っている, and it is not taught yet.

持, 待, 時 and 寺 (hold, wait, time and temple)

  • All four have 寺 on the right.
  • 持 (hold) has the hand radical 扌: you hold with your hand.
  • 待 (wait) has the step radical 彳.
  • 時 (time, from Kanji 2) has the sun 日.

閉, 開, 聞 and 間 (the gate kanji)

  • All four are a gate 門 with something inside.
  • 閉 (close) has 才 inside, like a bar across the gate.
  • 開 (open) has 开 inside, two hands opening it.
  • 聞 (hear) has an ear 耳 inside.
  • 間 (between, from Kanji 2) has the sun 日 inside.

知, 和, 味 and 矢 (know and its look-alikes)

  • 知 (know) is an arrow 矢 next to a mouth 口.
  • 和 and 味 were wrong choices for 知りません. They are not taught yet.

学 and 字 (study and letter)

  • 学 (study) has three short strokes and a crown on top.
  • 字 (letter) has a roof 宀 instead. 字先 and 字生 were wrong choices for 学生.

会, 全 and 合 (meet and its look-alikes)

  • 会 (meet) has 二 and a small hook under the roof.
  • 全 and 合 were wrong choices for 会います. They are not taught yet.

使, 便, 吏 and 更 (use and its look-alikes)

  • 使 (use) is the person radical 亻 next to 吏.
  • 便, 吏 and 更 were wrong choices for 使います. They are not taught yet.

作 and 昨 (make and yesterday)

  • 作 (make) has the person radical 亻.
  • 昨 (yesterday) has the sun 日 instead. It is not taught yet.
  • 作る takes only る: 作くります was a wrong choice.

言, 語, 話 and 読 (the speech kanji)

  • 言 (say) is also the speech radical on the left of 語, 話 and 読.
  • 語 (language) adds 吾, 話 (talk) adds 舌 (tongue), and 読 (read) adds 売 (sell, from Kanji 3).

話, 舌, 活 and 括 (talk and the tongue kanji)

  • 話 (talk) is speech 言 with a tongue 舌.
  • 活 has water 氵 and 括 has the hand 扌. Both were wrong choices for はなし, and they are not taught yet.

店, 点, 占 and 居 (store and its look-alikes)

  • 店 (store) is 占 under a roof 广.
  • 点, 占 and 居 were wrong choices for みせ. They are not taught yet.

国, 玉, 回 and 園 (country and the box kanji)

  • 国 (country) is a jewel 玉 inside a box.
  • 回 and 園 also sit inside a box. 玉 alone was a wrong choice too.

家, 族, 旅 and 像 (house and its look-alikes)

  • 家 (house) is a pig 豕 under a roof 宀.
  • 族, 旅 and 像 were wrong choices for いえ. They are not taught yet.

車, 重, 連 and 乗 (car and its look-alikes)

  • 車 (car) looks like a cart from above: wheels on an axle.
  • 重, 連 and 乗 were wrong choices for くるま. They are not taught yet.

方, 万, 力 and 刀 (direction and its look-alikes)

  • 方 (direction) has a dot on top.
  • 万 (ten thousand, from Kanji 1) has a flat bar on top and no dot.
  • 力 (power) and 刀 (knife) have no top bar.

駅, 馬, 鳥 and 訳 (station and the horse)

  • 駅 (station) is a horse 馬 with 尺 on the right: horses once waited at stations.
  • 鳥 (bird) and 訳 were wrong choices for えき. They are not taught yet.

道, 首, 週 and 周 (road and its look-alikes)

  • 道 (road) is 首 (head) on the walking radical 辶.
  • 週 (week, from Kanji 2) is 周 on the same radical.

校, 交 and 文 (school and its look-alikes)

  • 校 (school) is a tree 木 next to 交.
  • 交長, 父長 and 文長 were wrong choices for 校長.

都 and 部 (metropolis and part)

  • 都 (metropolis) has 者 on the left.
  • 部, 限 and 郊 were wrong choices for 東京都. They are not taught yet.

Readings of 入 (enter): はい, い, いり, にゅう

  • はい in 入る and い in 入れる.
  • いり in 入口 (いりぐち).
  • にゅう in 入学.

Readings of 出 (exit): だ, で, しゅつ

  • だ in 出す, で in 出る and 出かける.
  • しゅつ in 外出.

Readings of 止 (stop): と, し

  • と in 止める and 止まる.
  • し in 中止.

Readings of 切 (cut): き, きっ, せつ

  • き in 切る and きっ in 切手 (きって).
  • せつ in 大切な and しん切な.

Readings of 学 (study): まな, がく, がっ

  • まな in 学ぶ.
  • がく in 学生, 大学 and 見学, but がっ in 学校.

Readings of 会 (meet): あ, かい

  • あ in 会う.
  • かい in 会話, 会長 and 会社, and in 社会 (しゃかい).

Readings of 着 (wear, arrive): き, つ, ぎ

  • き in 着る (wear) and つ in 着く (arrive).
  • ぎ in 上着 (うわぎ).

Readings of 使 (use): つか, し

  • つか in 使う and 使い方.
  • し in 使よう.

Readings of 作 (make): つく, さく, さっ

  • つく in 作る.
  • さく in 作ぶん, but さっ in 作家.

Readings of 言 (say): い, こと, げん

  • い in 言う and こと in 言ば.
  • げん in 言語.

Readings of 語 (language): がたり, ご

  • がたり in もの語 (ものがたり).
  • ご in 言語, 日本語 and 英語.

Readings of 話 (talk): はな, はなし, わ

  • はな in 話す and はなし for 話 on its own.
  • わ in 電話 and 会話.

Readings of 店 (store): みせ, てん

  • みせ for 店 on its own.
  • てん in 店員, 本店 and 売店.

Readings of 国 (country): くに, こく, ごく

  • くに for 国 on its own.
  • こく in 外国 and 外国人, but ごく in 中国.

Readings of 家 (house): いえ, うち, か

  • いえ or うち for 家 on its own.
  • か in 作家 and 家ぞく.

Readings of 都 (metropolis): と, つ

  • と in 京都 and 東京都.
  • つ in 都ごう (つごう).

Readings of 方 (direction): かた, がた, ほう

  • かた in 方 (person) and 読み方, がた in ゆう方.
  • ほう in 右の方 and 方ほう.

Learning these in pairs helps, because each member reminds you of the other.
